blocks.text: Cybersecurity awareness means understanding how to protect computers, networks, and data from attacks. As people rely more on technology, cyber threats have become common in daily life. Hackers use tricks and harmful software to steal information or damage systems. Being aware of these dangers helps users stay alert and act safely online. Knowing how to detect, prevent, and respond to threats keeps personal and organizational data secure. For example, users should install antivirus software to protect their computers from malware and other security threats. They should also avoid using public Wi-Fi for online banking or other sensitive work because public networks may not be secure.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Avoid offensive language, spam, and sharing confidential information.
Understanding Cyber Threats

Cyber threats are actions or programs that target computers and networks to cause harm. These include stealing information, damaging systems, or interrupting online services. Understanding how threats work helps users recognize early warning signs. Most attacks can be avoided by safe browsing, using antivirus software, and being cautious with emails and links. Recognizing threats is the first step toward protecting digital systems.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Phishing is among the most common attacks.
Common Types of Cyberattacks

There are different kinds of cyber threats. A virus spreads through infected files and can damage or delete data. Phishing tries to trick people into sharing passwords or personal details through fake emails or websites. Ransomware locks data and demands payment to unlock it, while spyware secretly collects user information. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks overload websites, making them crash.
How Cyberattacks Affect Individuals and Organizations

Cyberattacks can cause serious damage to both individuals and organizations. People may lose personal files, passwords, or money, while companies may face data breaches and loss of customer trust. Attacks can stop business operations, harm reputations, and lead to financial losses. Even schools and hospitals can be affected by cyber incidents.
Security Tools and Techniques

Security tools and techniques help protect computers and networks from online threats. They make it harder for hackers or malicious software to access important information. These tools include authentication systems, firewalls, and antivirus programs that check and block harmful activities. Using them properly keeps personal data safe and reduces the chances of cyberattacks. Every computer user should understand and apply these tools to maintain digital safety.
Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) is a security method that requires two forms of verification before allowing access to an account. For example, after entering a password, the user may receive a code on their phone or email to confirm their identity. This extra step makes it much harder for hackers to break in.
Biometric Verification

Biometric verification uses physical features such as fingerprints, face scans, or voice patterns to verify identity. Biometrics add strong layers of protection to keep accounts and personal data safe.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students simulate logging into an account with a second step (code from teacher) to understand how 2FA works.
Use of Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (Ids), and Antivirus Tools

A firewall acts as a barrier between a computer and the internet, allowing safe data to pass while blocking harmful traffic. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) monitor networks for suspicious activities and alert users about possible threats. Antivirus software scans files and removes viruses or malware before they cause damage. Together, these tools form a powerful defense against cyberattacks. Using them regularly ensures that computers and networks remain protected and run smoothly.
Data Protection and Cryptography
Data protection means keeping digital information safe from unauthorized access, loss, or damage. It ensures that only the right people can view or use the data.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Secure storage and transmission prevent unauthorized access and breaches.

Cryptography is the science of securing information so that only authorized users can understand it. It consists of two core concepts such as encryption and decryption. Encryption changes readable data into coded text using a specific key, while decryption converts it back into its original form when needed. For example, when sending a message online, encryption makes it unreadable to anyone who tries to intercept it. This process ensures that information remains private during transmission. Cryptography is widely used in secure websites, online banking, and messaging apps.
Secure Methods for Transmitting and Storing Data

Data must be protected not only when stored on a computer but also when sent over the internet. Secure methods such as encrypted connections (like HTTPS) keep information safe during transmission. Cloud storage services also use encryption to prevent unauthorized access to saved files. Regular backups help protect data from loss caused by system failure or attacks. Following secure storage and transfer methods ensures that important data remains safe and reliable.
Detecting and Preventing Intrusions

Detecting and preventing intrusions means identifying and stopping unauthorized access to a computer or network. Cyber intrusions can occur when hackers exploit weaknesses to steal data or damage systems. Monitoring tools and security software help track unusual activity that might indicate an attack. Students learn how early detection prevents major losses and keeps systems running safely. Staying alert and updating security measures are key steps to maintaining protection against intrusions.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students look at sample system logs or screenshots to find suspicious actions.
Identifying Vulnerabilities and Suspicious Activities

Vulnerabilities are weaknesses in software, hardware, or user behavior that hackers can exploit. Suspicious activities may include unexpected system slowdowns, unknown programs running, or strange network traffic. Regularly checking system logs and using scanning tools can help find these warning signs. Recognizing patterns of unusual behavior allows users to take quick action. Identifying and fixing vulnerabilities early reduces the chance of successful attacks.
Applying Troubleshooting and Preventive Measures

When a security issue is found, troubleshooting helps determine its cause and how to fix it. Preventive measures include installing firewalls, antiviruses and anti-malware, updating software, changing passwords, or removing harmful files. In some cases, restoring data from backups may be necessary. Documenting the problem and the steps taken helps prevent it from happening again.
